flashcards.definition: Principal connective tissue cells synthesizing extracellular ground substance, collagen, and elastin fibers.
Connective tissue immune cells secreting Histamine (vasodilator), Heparin (anticoagulant), and Serotonin.
Phagocytic monocyte-derived cells that engulf foreign pathogens and cellular debris in connective tissue matrix.
Differentiated B-lymphocytes with 'cartwheel' nuclear chromatin that synthesize circulating antibodies.
Matrix under skin containing fibroblasts, mast cells, macrophages, collagen, and elastic fibers forming body packing.
Monolocular fat cells storing triglycerides for long-term energy storage and mechanical cushioning.
Multilocular fat cells packed with mitochondria expressing UCP-1 (Thermogenin) for non-shivering thermogenesis.
Dense regular white fibrous CT containing parallel Type I collagen bundles connecting skeletal muscle to bone.
Yellow elastic CT containing branching elastic fibers connecting bone to bone across joints.
Avascular solid pliable chondrin matrix with chondrocytes in lacunae; lines bone articular ends, nose, and ribs.
Toughest cartilage rich in Type I collagen bundles; lacks perichondrium; forms intervertebral discs.
Functional unit of compact bone comprising central Haversian canal, concentric ossein lamellae, lacunae, and canaliculi.
Transverse vascular channels connecting adjacent Haversian canals with periosteal blood vessels in compact bone.
Non-nucleated biconcave blood discs packed with hemoglobin carrying oxygen in peripheral circulation.
Nucleated immune blood cells split into Granulocytes (Neutrophils, Eosinophils, Basophils) and Agranulocytes (Monocytes, Lymphocytes).
